thesis: Altria Group (MO) is the largest U.S. tobacco company. **[Fact]** It sells Marlboro cigarettes and Black & Mild cigars through Philip Morris USA and John Middleton; Copenhagen, Skoal, and on! oral nicotine products through U.S. Smokeless Tobacco and Helix; and NJOY e-vapor devices through the all-other category. **[Fact]** FY2025 net revenues were **$23.3 billion** (down 3.1% versus 2024), with smokeable products at **$20.5 billion** and oral tobacco at **$2.8 billion**. **[Fact]** The company also holds a roughly **10%** stake in Anheuser-Busch InBev (ABI), accounted for under the equity method with a one-quarter lag. Altria returns most free cash flow as dividends and buybacks.
why_market_wrong: The market prices Altria as a melting ice cube: volumes fall, ESG funds cannot own the stock, and litigation risk never fully clears. **[Fact]** Smokeable cigarette shipment volume fell **10.0%** in 2025, yet smokeable operating companies income (OCI) rose to **$10.98 billion** because pricing and mix held. **[Inference]** Generalists may underweight the oral nicotine pouch transition (on!) and the bond-like cash yield at today's price. There is no dated predictive attribute (Horizon Kinetics equity yield curve); the inefficiency is **descriptive** (sin-stock exclusion, volume-decline narrative) rather than a timed catalyst.
